content: # Design a NetSuite FreeMarker Template Use this skill before producing or revising a complete FreeMarker draft. The goal is a faithful rendered document, not a recognizable generic approximation. ## Authority and judgment Apply this priority: explicit user instructions; observed reference evidence; verified brand/account facts; skills as implementation guidance; general preferences. Skills provide methods, not visual facts. Treat every suggested corner, radius, icon style, color, spacing rule, and composition as a candidate. Apply it only where the reference supports it and only at the observed scope. Never propagate a local motif merely for consistency. ## Required workflow 1. Load the current Template Studio session, including `startingPoint`, `assetToolsEnabled`, references, source, render state, and feedback. 2. Load relevant local skills and apply them under the authority order above. 3. For an uploaded template, preserve its source, render it if needed, and inspect every page before editing. Do not replace it with a generic rewrite. 4. For a photographed, skewed, or multi-page mockup, isolate the intended page and conceptually normalize its page rectangle before measuring. Ignore surrounding surfaces and duplicate sheets. 5. Complete the reference decomposition and asset decision gates before writing source or creating any asset. 6. Build or patch a complete BFO-compatible `` document. 7. Treat the first render as a diagnostic measurement pass. Capture page 1, inspect every page, complete the deviation audit, patch material differences, and rerender. 8. When a technical behavior is uncertain or a tested construction fails, complete the research escalation gate before declaring a limitation or switching to an asset workaround. ## Reference decomposition gate Create a compact internal fidelity plan containing: - page aspect ratio, major regions, columns, margins, and region boundaries as page-relative ratios; - every distinctive landmark and its approximate `x/pageWidth`, `y/pageHeight`, `width/pageWidth`, and `height/pageHeight`; - landmark colors, geometry, repetition count, visual hierarchy, and exact local motif scope; - a reproduction classification for each visual: native BFO structure, reuse exact asset, faithful SVG, or unresolved. Do not start from a generic invoice and decorate it afterward. Do not silently omit inconvenient landmarks. ## Asset decision gate Asset tooling is optional, not the default construction method. Before any asset call, classify the target: - Use native BFO/FreeMarker tables, nested cells, backgrounds, borders, padding, explicit dimensions, and document-flow structure for panels, bands, pills, rules, simple corner blocks, repeated dots, contact-icon circles, and other basic geometry. - Use BFO-native barcode/QR output only when the required real value is known. Never fabricate a decorative QR value. - Reuse or create an asset only for irreducible artwork such as a supplied logo, handwriting/signature, or genuinely complex vector motif required by the reference. - Never create a generic semantic substitute for a distinctive logo, icon, signature, or pattern. Faithfully reproduce it, reuse exact supplied artwork, or report it unresolved. If `assetToolsEnabled` is false, do not call any asset tool and do not inspect asset metadata. Existing placeholders may continue to render. Solve geometry natively or report only a genuinely irreducible missing-artwork requirement. If asset tools are enabled, call the asset list only after this gate identifies a justified need. Do not create more assets while major page geometry is wrong. ## BFO alternatives before declaring a limitation Lack of browser layering, negative offsets, or per-corner CSS is not itself a stopping point. Try at least two materially different BFO-safe constructions and evaluate their renders, such as: - split geometry into adjoining table cells or rows; - restructure source order and use nested full-width tables to create an overlap illusion in document flow; - compose the silhouette from background-colored cells, borders, padding, and exact row heights; - reserve a measured decoration column or row instead of floating approximately. Use an SVG mask only after native constructions and the research gate fail, only when asset tools are enabled, and only if its render is closer. Judge workarounds by fidelity, not cleverness. ## Technical research escalation gate Research is mandatory when BFO/FreeMarker behavior is uncertain, a render contradicts expectations, two native constructions fail, or you are about to say a feature is unsupported. Use whichever documentation or internet-search tools the current host provides; this instruction is tool-name independent for Codex and Claude Code compatibility. 1. Form a narrow technical question from the observed render, including the exact BFO element/CSS property/FreeMarker behavior and failure symptom. 2. Search primary sources first: Oracle NetSuite Help or SuiteAnswers when accessible, the Big Faceless PDF Library user guide/API documentation, and the official FreeMarker manual. Search broader web sources only to locate a primary source or a reproducible workaround. 3. Open and read the supporting page; a search-result snippet is not evidence. Record the source title or URL, applicable constraint, and a testable hypothesis. 4. Build the smallest isolated experiment inside the current template, render it, and compare the result. A documented feature is not proven for NetSuite's embedded BFO version until the render confirms it. 5. If research disproves the approach, try the documented alternative. Do not respond by generating an asset unless the asset decision gate independently justifies one. Never claim `BFO cannot do this`, `FreeMarker does not support this`, or similar without either primary-source evidence plus a render test, or a reproducible test showing the limitation. If the host has no browsing/documentation capability or access fails, state that research was unavailable and continue with local documentation and controlled render experiments; never invent a source or pretend research occurred. ## SVG sizing and padding - Asset dimensions control aspect ratio and raster density; every FreeMarker `` needs explicit `width` and `height` derived from the normalized reference. - Keep `viewBox` tight around visible artwork. Match the display-box aspect ratio unless intentional cropping is visible; use `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"` for uncropped artwork. - Rasterize above display resolution for sharpness without changing physical PDF size. - For an upright icon in a 45-degree rotated square, use a 50-58% glyph safe area and optical centering only when the reference contains that construction. - Compare visible artwork bounds, not just the image box. Fix SVG viewBox/padding for internal-bound errors; fix FreeMarker width/height for whole-box errors. ## Dimension-first render review After each render, compare normalized landmark boxes against the reference. Record the largest structural deltas first: page regions, header/footer height, column split, table start/end, dominant whitespace, and landmark scale. Correct those before typography polish or decorative assets. Use explicit dimensions and ratios; do not rely on `looks close`. When the render differs materially, propose and try an alternative construction. A `known deltas` list is not acceptance and does not justify stopping. Continue until differences are resolved, the user accepts them, or a limitation remains after research and tested alternatives. ## Fidelity rules - Match composition, silhouettes, region boundaries, proportions, and landmark placement before typography. - Preserve grouping semantics: a continuous rounded table is not equivalent to separate pills, and a corner decoration is not a reusable card radius. - Match significant repetition exactly: dot grids, dividers, icons, row treatment, and motif count. - Do not simplify, modernize, rebalance, or make the design more consistent unless asked. - Never invent a logo, legal claim, tax value, customer datum, or NetSuite field mapping. ## BFO and FreeMarker constraints - Emit well-formed XML with the XML declaration, BFO report doctype, one ``, one ``, and one ``. - Prefer tables for page layout. Do not use browser-only CSS, JavaScript, or inline base64 images. - Use conservative BFO-compatible CSS with explicit dimensions, font sizes, line heights, padding, borders, widths, and alignment. - Escape XML-sensitive characters and keep FreeMarker expressions valid inside XML. - Use stable sample values for freestyle sessions. Bind record fields only when proven by metadata or a loaded binding skill. ## Mandatory deviation audit After every reference-led render, check every fidelity-plan item: normalized geometry, missing/substituted assets, motif scope, visible asset bounds, colors, typography scale, whitespace, table continuity, repetition counts, clipping, pagination, and footer structure. Classify each mismatch as source layout, SVG geometry, asset display size, missing artwork, or uncertain platform behavior. Patch the correct layer and rerender. Route uncertain platform behavior through the research gate. The first render is never accepted merely because it is recognizable. Before presenting, report only deliberate differences and limitations remaining after research and tested alternatives.
